goldens.comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:189 — No test covers the catch-block retryCount increment on thrown errors, leaving the failure-path update (data race with the else-branch update, duplicate update potential) unverified

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a `retryCount` field and increments it in two distinct paths: the `else` branch when `scheduledSMS` is falsy, and the `catch` block on thrown errors. These paths are mutually exclusive in a single execution, so the stated “data race with the else-branch update / duplicate update potential” isn’t supported by the shown code. Also, the claim that “no test covers the catch-block” cannot be verified from this PR diff because no test files or test changes are shown (tests could exist elsewhere).
